title: Zero-Copy Vectorization Pipelines in WebAssembly
summary: Exploring shared memory buffers and SIMD vector instructions inside browser runtimes for instantaneous SVG path decimation and raster processing.
content:
### Introduction

Vector graphics decimation and Bezier curve smoothing typically require heavy round-trips to backend GPU clusters or sluggish JavaScript DOM traversals that drop frame rates on complex architectural blueprints.

### Shared Memory Architecture in WebAssembly

DetailMint leverages direct WebAssembly linear memory allocation to operate directly on raw vertex buffers without serialization penalties:

1. **Zero-Copy Memory Transfer**: Direct pointer arithmetic over typed array views.
2. **SIMD-Accelerated Curve Smoothing**: 128-bit vector registers evaluate cubic Bezier inflection points in parallel across 4 points per cycle.
3. **Memory Footprint**: Sub-10MB peak memory footprint even when processing 500k-vertex technical schematics.

### Production Outcomes

This architecture powers our browser-based design tools, delivering instantaneous 60fps previews on low-power mobile devices.
